title: Antarctica Field Trip To Mertz Glacier
titleZh: 南极默茨冰川实地考察

parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Part four. You will hear part of a talk given by a researcher about a recent field trip to a glacier in Antarctica.

First, you have some time to look at questions thirty-one to forty.

Now listen carefully and answer questions thirty-one to forty.

Good afternoon, everyone. Today, I'd like to talk to you about our recent field trip to the Mertz Glacier in Antarctica, and to place it in the wider context of research and international cooperation.

According to the Antarctic Treaty, the whole region was designated for the advancement of science and maintaining global peace.

This decision was a milestone in international cooperation, preventing conflict in one of the world's most isolated areas. The treaty has provided a framework that allows nations to collaborate rather than compete, and it is one of the reasons why Antarctica remains such a unique site for fieldwork. Now, preparing for an expedition to such an environment requires great care. The explorers always had to pack spare batteries to keep their instruments functioning in the harsh climate. Without them, they risked losing valuable data during research missions.

In addition, it was equally important that they could operate a radio device in case of emergencies.

Radios were often the only way to contact nearby stations for help, so every member of the team was given basic communication training before departure.

The journey itself began with sea travel. The team traveled aboard the Aurora Australia, a modern research vessel that even has its own library for study and reference. This facility allowed the scientists to continue reading, analyzing, and preparing reports while at sea.

On arrival, the schedule was filled with both practical work and training. During their stay, they attended specialized workshops that offered guidance on managing and preserving scientific data.

These sessions helped ensure that valuable findings would be stored accurately and shared effectively with other researchers.

Once the field activities began, the scientists undertook a variety of monitoring tasks.

One of their tasks involved monitoring water pollution, particularly measuring how much acid was present in the environment.

Careful recording of acidity levels was essential for tracking long-term changes in ocean health.

Alongside this, they also carried out inspections of the instruments used in a penguin study, including checking that the cameras were functioning correctly.

Reliable footage was vital for observing penguin behavior without disturbing the animals directly. Speaking of penguins, one of the most fascinating observations came from their movements.

Researchers observed that penguin colonies often advance across the ice, forming a pattern like a wave.

This movement not only creates rhythm in their march but also provides protection and energy efficiency for the group. The recordings captured by the cameras gave the team new insights into these collective behaviors. Of course, environmental issues were also a major focus. Scientists carefully recorded the specific types of rubbish discovered in the environment. Analyzing this debris allowed them to identify the zones most seriously affected by human pollution and to make recommendations for cleaning and protecting sensitive areas.

Finally, we should mention the plans for the future. Plans are underway for an additional ship that will serve future expeditions. This modern vessel is expected to provide improved laboratories and accommodation, making research far more efficient. It will also allow larger teams to visit Antarctica and extend the reach of collaborative projects. So to summarize, the trip to the Mertz Glacier was not only about data collection, but also about training, cooperation, and planning for sustainable research in one of the harshest environments on Earth.

That is the end of part four. You now have forty-five seconds to check your answers to part four.

analyses.content: 录音里明确提到南极条约（Antarctic Treaty）将该地区用于科学发展（science）和维护全球和平（peace），刚好对应题目的两个并列信息。
你可能会把“global peace”都写上，但注意题目字数要求是“ONE WORD ONLY”，所以只能填最核心的名词“peace”。

Today, I'd like to talk to you about our recent field trip to the Mertz Glacier in Antarctica, and to place it in the wider context of research and international cooperation. According to the Antarctic Treaty, the whole region was designated for the advancement of science and maintaining global peace.
录音中用“pack spare（打包备用的）”替换了题干的“take extra（带额外的）”，后面紧跟着的“batteries”就是设备所需带上的物品。
你可能会听到后面的“data”而填错，但“data”是没带电池会导致丢失的东西，而不是为了设备额外带的东西。

Now, preparing for an expedition to such an environment requires great care. The explorers always had to pack spare batteries to keep their instruments functioning in the harsh climate. Without them, they risked losing valuable data during research missions.
录音中说的“operate a radio device in case of emergencies（在紧急情况下操作无线电）”完美对应了题干的“use a _____ for emergencies”。
你可能想填“device”，但“radio”才是体现具体沟通用途的核心词，且填入“radio”更符合语境。

In addition, it was equally important that they could operate a radio device in case of emergencies. Radios were often the only way to contact nearby stations for help, so every member of the team was given basic communication training before departure.
录音里提到Aurora Australia这艘船“has its own library”，这跟题干上的“has its own”一模一样，听到就可以直接锁定答案。
这里基本就是送分题，别被后面补充说明的“study and reference”分散注意力导致漏听或拼错即可。

The journey itself began with sea travel. The team traveled aboard the Aurora Australia, a modern research vessel that even has its own library for study and reference. This facility allowed the scientists to continue reading, analyzing, and preparing reports while at sea.
题干里的“advice”在录音里换了个说法变成了“guidance”，紧随其后的“managing and preserving”原词重现，顺理成章带出答案“data”。
你可能会听到完整的“scientific data”而不知道怎么填，但字数限制只有一个词，所以果断舍弃形容词提取核心名词“data”即可。

On arrival, the schedule was filled with both practical work and training. During their stay, they attended specialized workshops that offered guidance on managing and preserving scientific data. These sessions helped ensure that valuable findings would be stored accurately and shared effectively with other researchers.
录音用“measuring”替换了题目的“monitoring”，紧跟着的“how much acid was present”直接解答了“how much ______ there was”的疑问。
注意不要填成后面补充说明里出现的“acidity levels”，根据疑问词“how much”锁定不可数名词“acid”是最稳妥的。

One of their tasks involved monitoring water pollution, particularly measuring how much acid was present in the environment. Careful recording of acidity levels was essential for tracking long-term changes in ocean health.
录音先提到了“penguin study”，然后用“including checking”引出具体检查的设备，答案“cameras”呼之欲出。
这题答案带有复数“s”，听的时候一定要注意抓尾音，别只写了单数“camera”导致冤枉扣分。

Alongside this, they also carried out inspections of the instruments used in a penguin study, including checking that the cameras were functioning correctly. Reliable footage was vital for observing penguin behavior without disturbing the animals directly.
题干的“in the shape of（以...的形状）”被替换成了“forming a pattern like（形成像...一样的图案）”，后面紧跟的“a wave”就是正确答案。
你可能只顾着死等“shape”这个词而错过了“pattern”这种换汤不换药的说法，导致跟丢了后面的正确答案。

Speaking of penguins, one of the most fascinating observations came from their movements. Researchers observed that penguin colonies often advance across the ice, forming a pattern like a wave. This movement not only creates rhythm in their march but also provides protection and energy efficiency for the group.
题干的“Noting details of（记录...的细节）”换了个说法变成了“carefully recorded the specific types of”，直接引出后面的记录对象“rubbish”。
你可能会听到下一句出现的“debris”或者后面的“human pollution”，但只有“rubbish”是紧跟在“记录”这个动作后面的第一对象。

Of course, environmental issues were also a major focus. Scientists carefully recorded the specific types of rubbish discovered in the environment. Analyzing this debris allowed them to identify the zones most seriously affected by human pollution and to make recommendations for cleaning and protecting sensitive areas.
录音明确提到正在计划一艘额外的船（an additional ship），这里的“additional”和后面说的“modern vessel”都对应题干的“new”，所以填“ship”或“vessel”都对。
你可能会听到后面的“laboratories”并想把它填进去，但实验室是这艘船提供的内部设施，而题目问的是整体计划了一个新的“什么”。

Finally, we should mention the plans for the future. Plans are underway for an additional ship that will serve future expeditions. This modern vessel is expected to provide improved laboratories and accommodation, making research far more efficient.
